observations: StateFingerprint deliberately exposes two non-equivalent predicates: projection_changed compares typed projection content while identity_changed includes generation/identity movement.
For identical typed projection bytes with generation advanced, projection_changed is false while identity_changed is true.
F2-WP-206 explicitly requires projection-change versus lineage-change policy to remain explicit across persistence/restart.
Persistent Pulse accepts explicit candidate references but does not itself know which fingerprint-change semantics produced them.
risk: If WP206 persists only a boolean changed signal or a candidate reference while omitting the selected fingerprint-change policy from the checkpoint/replay identity, a restart can silently reinterpret the same fingerprint pair under different semantics. A generation-only transition can then change from no-change to changed (or vice versa) without any payload change, yielding false next-tick equivalence or wake eligibility. A generic changed=true signal could also be over-promoted into ACT/DELEGATE eligibility without preserving the caller's explicit semantic choice.
hypothesis: Persist the selected change policy as a typed enum/value inside the canonical Agency checkpoint payload and include it in the checkpoint digest and next-tick identity. Recompute the predicate from the verified pre/post StateFingerprint pair after restart; do not persist or trust a free-floating changed boolean as authoritative. Keep any ACT/DELEGATE candidate reference separately caller-supplied and provenance-bound; fingerprint change alone is not effect authority.
counterhypothesis: If WP206 never persists/replays a fingerprint-derived change decision and always reconstructs both policy and candidate references from a higher-level canonical policy object whose exact digest is already bound into the checkpoint, duplicating the policy inside the Agency checkpoint may be unnecessary. That higher-level binding must be explicit and tested before relying on it.
cheapest_discriminators: Create two fingerprints with identical projection schema/content and generations N and N+1: projection_changed must be false and identity_changed true; restart replay must preserve whichever policy was selected before exit.
Keep the same fingerprint pair but mutate the persisted change-policy field between process runs: checkpoint digest/next-tick identity must change or replay must fail closed.
Persist only changed=true in a negative fixture and omit policy identity: loader/replay must reject it as ambiguous instead of defaulting to projection_changed or identity_changed.
A fingerprint-derived changed signal without an independently explicit ACT/DELEGATE candidate reference must never manufacture ACT/DELEGATE eligibility.
next_exact_action: Active F2-WP-206 mutation authority should bind the selected StateFingerprint change policy into the typed checkpoint/replay identity and add the generation-only discriminator before claiming restart/next-tick acceptance.
